2: For the music director, according to The Lilies. Of David. Save me, O God, because waters have come up to my neck.
3: I sink in the mud of the deep, and there is no foothold. I have come to watery depths, and the torrent floods over me.
4: I am weary with my calling out; my throat is parched. My eyes are exhausted in my waiting for my God.
5: More numerous than the hairs of my head are those hating me without a cause. Those who are destroying me—my enemies wrongfully— are mighty. What I did not steal, I then must restore.
6: O God, ⌞you yourself know⌟ my foolishness, and my guilty deeds are not hidden from you.
7: Let those who wait for you not be put to shame because of me, O Lord Yahweh of hosts. Let those who seek you not be disgraced because of me, O God of Israel.
8: Because on account of you I have borne reproach; disgrace has covered my face.
9: I have become a stranger to my brothers and a foreigner to my mother’s sons,
10: because the zeal for your house has consumed me, and the reproaches of those reproaching you have fallen on me.
11: When I wept in the fasting of my soul, it became reproaches for me.
12: When I made sackcloth my clothing, I became for them a byword.
13: Those sitting at the gate talk about me as also the songs of the drunkards.
14: But as for me, my prayer is to you, O Yahweh, for a favorable time, O God, according to the abundance of your loyal love. Answer me with the faithfulness of your salvation.
15: Deliver me from the mud and do not let me sink. Let me be delivered from those who hate me and from the watery depths.
16: Do not let the torrent of waters flood over me, or the deep swallow me, or the pit close its mouth over me.
17: Answer me, O Yahweh, because your loyal love is good; according to your abundant mercies, turn to me,
18: and do not hide your face from your servant. Because I am in trouble, answer me quickly.
19: Draw near to my soul; redeem it. Because of my enemies, ransom me.
20: You know my reproach, my shame and my disgrace. ⌞Fully known⌟ to you are all my adversaries.
21: Reproach has broken my heart and I am sick. And I hoped for sympathy, but there was none, and for comforters, but I found none.
22: They also gave me gall for food, and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
23: Let their table before them be a trap, and their times of peace a snare.
24: Let their eyes be dark so they cannot see, and make their loins continually tremble.
25: Pour out your indignation on them, and let your burning anger overtake them.
26: Let their camp be desolate. Let none dwell in their tents,
27: because they persecute those whom you, yourself, have struck, and they tell of the pain of those you have wounded.
28: ⌞Add guilt on top of their guilt⌟, and do not let them ⌞be acquitted⌟.
29: Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and let them not be recorded with the righteous.
30: But as for me, though I am afflicted and pained, your salvation will protect me, O God.
31: I will praise the name of God in song, and magnify him with thanksgiving.
32: For Yahweh it will be better than an ox or bull, horned and hoofed.
33: The afflicted will see and rejoice. O God seekers, let your heart revive,
34: because Yahweh hears the needy and does not despise his own who are prisoners.
35: Let heavens and earth praise him, the seas and all that moves in them,
36: because God will save Zion and build the cities of Judah, that they may dwell there and possess it.
37: And the offspring of his servants will inherit it, and those who love his name will abide in it.
